qa_pairs.question: For Fall 2026, when do classes begin and when does the standard add/drop period end?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: For Fall 2026, classes begin on August 17 and the standard add/drop period ends at 17:00 on August 28.

contexts.text: For Fall 2026, priority registration opens on July 20, regular registration closes on August 14, classes begin on August 17, and the standard add/drop period ends at 17:00 on August 28.

qa_pairs.question: How much is undergraduate tuition per credit for 2026-2027, and how much is the student-services fee in Fall?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: Undergraduate tuition for the 2026-2027 academic year is USD 420 per registered credit, and the student-services fee is USD 180 in Fall.

contexts.text: Undergraduate tuition for the 2026–2027 academic year is USD 420 per registered credit. The student-services fee is USD 180 in Fall and Spring and USD 90 in Summer.

qa_pairs.question: What minimum attendance rate is expected, and may a course syllabus set a lower threshold?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: Students are expected to attend at least 80% of scheduled sessions in courses that record attendance. A course syllabus may set a higher threshold, but it may not set a lower threshold.

contexts.text: Students are expected to attend at least 80% of scheduled sessions in courses that record attendance. A course syllabus may set a higher threshold when required by accreditation, laboratory safety, or clinical practice, but it may not set a lower threshold.

qa_pairs.question: How many verified internship hours are required, and do hours completed before approval count?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: Programmes with an internship requirement require at least 240 verified hours, and hours completed before approval do not normally count.

contexts.text: Programmes with an internship requirement require at least 240 verified hours. Before starting, the student must have an approved placement agreement and workplace supervisor. Hours completed before approval do not normally count.

qa_pairs.question: What does the Northstar Merit Scholarship cover, and which charges does it not cover?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: The Northstar Merit Scholarship covers 50% of undergraduate tuition, but it does not cover student-services fees, late fees, or late-add fees.

contexts.text: The Northstar Merit Scholarship covers 50% of undergraduate tuition but does not cover student-services fees, late fees, or late-add fees.

qa_pairs.question: What approvals and payment does a late add require after standard add/drop ends, and what happens if the fee is not paid on time?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: A late add is allowed from the end of standard add/drop through the census date and requires instructor approval, programme-director approval, and payment of a USD 40 late-add fee per course within two business days of approval. Failure to pay on time cancels the late add, and the fee is non-refundable unless the university cancels the course or confirms an administrative error.

contexts.text: Version 2.0 introduces a late-add window from the end of standard add/drop through the census date. A late add requires instructor approval, programme-director approval, and payment of a USD 40 late-add fee per course within two business days of approval. Failure to pay on time cancels the late add.

The late-add fee is USD 40 per course and must be paid within two business days after the approvals described in `02_course_registration.md`. The late-add fee is non-refundable unless the university cancels the course or confirms an administrative error.

qa_pairs.question: If I drop one Fall 2026 course after standard add/drop but before the census date, how much tuition is reversed, and what changes after census?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: From the day after standard add/drop through the census date, 50% of that course's tuition is reversed. After census, no tuition is reversed for an ordinary course withdrawal. For Fall 2026 the census date is September 4.

contexts.text: For a course dropped by the end of standard add/drop, 100% of that course's tuition is reversed. From the day after standard add/drop through the census date, 50% is reversed. After census, no tuition is reversed for an ordinary course withdrawal.
The census date is September 4.

qa_pairs.question: My final grade was published and I believe the instructor made a calculation error. What steps and deadlines apply?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: A disagreement about academic judgement is handled first with the instructor, and you must request clarification from the instructor within five business days after the final grade is published. A formal grade appeal must be filed within ten business days after publication and must identify at least one permitted ground, such as calculation error, material departure from the published syllabus, procedural unfairness, or prohibited discrimination. Disagreement with academic judgement alone is not a permitted ground.

contexts.text: A disagreement about academic judgement is handled first with the instructor. Alleged calculation error, procedural unfairness, discrimination, or inconsistency with the published syllabus may proceed to the formal grade-appeal route in `08_student_support_and_appeals.md`.

The student must first request clarification from the instructor within five business days after the final grade is published. A formal grade appeal must be filed within ten business days after publication and must identify at least one permitted ground: calculation error, material departure from the published syllabus, procedural unfairness, or prohibited discrimination. Disagreement with academic judgement alone is not a permitted ground.

qa_pairs.question: What must a Merit Scholarship recipient achieve to renew the award, and how and when can a scholarship decision be appealed?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: To renew, a recipient must complete at least 12 graded Northstar credits in the reviewed term, earn a term GPA of at least 3.30, maintain a cumulative GPA of at least 3.20, and have no active serious-conduct sanction. A scholarship decision may be appealed within ten business days, and the appeal goes to the Financial Aid Review Committee.

contexts.text: To renew, a recipient must complete at least 12 graded Northstar credits in the reviewed term, earn a term GPA of at least 3.30, maintain a cumulative GPA of at least 3.20, and have no active serious-conduct sanction.
Scholarship decisions use the same ten-business-day filing window but go to the Financial Aid Review Committee.

qa_pairs.question: I missed the tuition due date and the grace period. What is charged, and can I still register for courses?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: A five-calendar-day grace period applies to the account balance. An unpaid balance after the grace period receives a USD 75 late-payment fee and a financial hold that blocks new registration, official transcripts, and graduation clearance, although it does not remove you from courses that were already confirmed. You may register again only when there is no active academic, conduct, advising, or financial hold.

contexts.text: A five-calendar-day grace period applies to the account balance, but it does not extend registration or scholarship deadlines.

An unpaid balance after the grace period receives a USD 75 late-payment fee and a financial hold. The hold blocks new registration, official transcripts, and graduation clearance. It does not remove a student from courses that were already confirmed.
A student may register only when there is no active academic, conduct, advising, or financial hold.

qa_pairs.question: If my medical leave is approved, what happens to my Merit Scholarship, and how is a voluntary leave for employment treated differently?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: A leave of absence pauses active enrolment while preserving your programme place, and a standard leave may last one or two consecutive regular terms. An approved medical leave pauses the scholarship for up to two consecutive regular terms and does not consume the one-term probation opportunity. A voluntary leave for employment or travel does not automatically reserve the award; you must request a scholarship deferral before the census date.

contexts.text: A leave of absence pauses active enrolment while preserving the student's programme place. A standard leave may last one or two consecutive regular terms.

An approved medical leave pauses the scholarship for up to two consecutive regular terms and does not consume the one-term probation opportunity. A voluntary leave for employment or travel does not automatically reserve the award; the student must request a scholarship deferral before the census date.

qa_pairs.question: I finished all coursework but still owe tuition. Can my degree be conferred and can I get my final transcript?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: No. Degree conferral also requires clearance of financial, library, conduct, and document holds. A financial hold does not erase completed academic requirements, but it blocks official conferral and release of the final transcript until the balance is resolved. The same financial hold also blocks new registration and official transcripts.

contexts.text: Degree conferral also requires clearance of financial, library, conduct, and document holds. A financial hold does not erase completed academic requirements, but it blocks official conferral and release of the final transcript until resolved under `03_tuition_payment_refund.md`.
The hold blocks new registration, official transcripts, and graduation clearance.

qa_pairs.question: A student first discussed a late add with the instructor in July 2026 but submitted the late-add request on August 20, 2026. Which registration policy version applies, what fee is charged, and how late may the add be made?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: Version 2.0 applies because the late-add request was made on or after August 1, 2026, even though the student first discussed it in July. Under version 2.0 the late-add window runs from the end of standard add/drop through the census date and the fee is USD 40 per course, not the USD 25 and seven-calendar-day window of version 1.0.

contexts.text: Registration Policy version 1.0, effective before August 1, 2026, allowed late adds for seven calendar days after standard add/drop and charged USD 25. Version 2.0, effective August 1, 2026, allows late adds only through census and charges USD 40 per course. A late-add request made on or after August 1, 2026 follows version 2.0 even if the student first discussed the request in July.
Version 2.0 introduces a late-add window from the end of standard add/drop through the census date.

qa_pairs.question: A Merit Scholarship holder failed one academic renewal requirement in Fall 2026, then withdrew from a course after the Spring 2027 census date and finished the term with only 9 completed graded credits. What happens to the award?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: The Fall failure normally produces one term of scholarship probation rather than immediate loss, and the award remains active during probation. The Spring withdrawal after census receives a `W` and still counts as attempted credit but not completed credit, so the student falls below the 12 completed graded credits required and fails the Spring review. A second consecutive failed review ends the award beginning with the next term.

contexts.text: A first failure to meet one academic renewal requirement normally produces one term of scholarship probation rather than immediate loss. During probation, the award remains active. A second consecutive failed review ends the award beginning with the next term.
A withdrawal after census still counts as attempted credit but not completed credit and may cause failure at the end-of-term review.
After census and through the withdrawal deadline in `01_academic_calendar.md`, the course receives a `W`.

qa_pairs.question: A student's last documented participation was September 20, 2026, and on November 10, 2026 they request a retroactive medical leave and a tuition refund. Is the request still filed in time, and what money can they receive?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: The request is outside the normal window: a retroactive medical request must normally be filed within 30 calendar days after the last documented participation, so a request filed on November 10 for participation that ended on September 20 requires evidence that the condition also prevented filing during that 30-day period. An approved medical withdrawal may receive a pro-rated tuition credit for future study calculated from the last documented date of participation; it is not a cash refund.

contexts.text: Medical leave may be approved retroactively when a documented condition prevented timely submission. A retroactive request must normally be filed within 30 calendar days after the student's last documented participation. Later requests require evidence that the condition also prevented filing during that 30-day period.

An approved medical withdrawal may receive a pro-rated tuition credit for future study, calculated from the last documented date of participation. It is not a cash refund and requires the process in `06_leave_and_withdrawal.md`.

qa_pairs.question: The portal was unavailable for three continuous hours during the final six hours before a published deadline, my home internet also failed, and I have an open appeal. Does the deadline move, and what time does it end?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: A deadline stated as a calendar date ends at 17:00 Northstar local time unless the policy explicitly gives another time. Because the portal was unavailable for more than two continuous hours during the final six hours before the deadline, the Registrar may announce a documented extension. An individual internet or device problem does not automatically extend a deadline, and an appeal pauses neither a payment deadline nor an academic deadline unless the responsible office grants a written temporary hold.

contexts.text: A deadline stated as a calendar date ends at 17:00 Northstar local time unless the policy explicitly gives another time. A submission received after the deadline is late even if a student started it earlier. When the student portal is unavailable for more than two continuous hours during the final six hours before a published deadline, the Registrar may announce a documented extension. Individual internet or device problems do not automatically extend a deadline.
An appeal pauses neither a payment deadline nor an academic deadline unless the responsible office grants a written temporary hold.

qa_pairs.question: A student has six credits remaining and a pending grade appeal in a course that affects a degree requirement. May they take part in commencement, and will the transcript show the degree?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: Students with no more than six credits remaining may request permission to participate early, but participation in a commencement ceremony is ceremonial and is not proof that a degree has been conferred; the transcript will not show the degree until every requirement and hold is cleared. A pending grade appeal may delay conferral if the disputed course affects a degree requirement or GPA threshold, and the department chair reviews a grade appeal first.

contexts.text: Participation in a commencement ceremony is ceremonial and is not proof that a degree has been conferred. Students with no more than six credits remaining may request permission to participate early, but the transcript will not show the degree until every requirement and hold is cleared.
A pending grade appeal may delay conferral if the disputed course affects a degree requirement or GPA threshold.
The department chair reviews a grade appeal first.

qa_pairs.expected_answer: The premise is incorrect. After census, no tuition is reversed for an ordinary course withdrawal; 100% is reversed only for a course dropped by the end of standard add/drop, and 50% from the day after standard add/drop through the census date. The assistant must not invent a policy, and it may explain a rule but cannot approve an exception or waive a fee, so the student should be directed to the responsible office.

contexts.text: The assistant must not invent a policy when the documents do not contain an answer.
